qt: Klausimas, į kurį atsakoma raštu, E-001067/2024 Komisijai Darbo tvarkos taisyklių 138 straipsnis Bronis Ropė (Verts/ALE) Tema:

Pasak Komisijos, jos parengtus žalinimo reikalavimus įgyvendino apie 96 proc. Lietuvos ūkininkų. Pagal LR žemės ūkio ministerijos parengtų ekoschemų (jos iš esmės turėjo pakeisti žalinimo reikalavimus) duomenis plotinėse ekoschemose dalyvavo vos 26 tūkst. pareiškėjų iš 114 tūkst. pateikusių paraiškas (23 proc.). Savo pastaboje Nr. 65 dėl LR strateginio plano Komisija nurodė: “ Lietuva turėtų peržiūrėti ir prireikus pertvarkyti savo siūlomas ekologines sistemas, kad būtų pagerinta įtraukta praktika, ir sutelkti dėmesį į tas intervencines priemones, kurios turi didesnę aplinkosauginę vertę. Tai sumažintų galimą riziką, kad skiriamos lėšos bus išsklaidytos tarp daugelio intervencinių priemonių ir taip prarastų veiksmingumą, o ūkininkai dažniausiai pasinaudotų mažiausiai plataus užmojo priemonėmis.“1 Pagal Reglamento 2021/2115 118 str. 3 dalį „Valstybė narė pateikia Komisijai visą reikiamą papildomą informaciją ir, kai tikslinga, patikslina pasiūlytą planą.“ Ar Komisija galėtų atsakyti į toliau pateiktus klausimus: 1.
Ar Komisija buvo prognozavusi tokius rezultatus, kad 3 iš 4 Lietuvos ūkininkų nedalyvavo ekoschemose?
Ar jie prisideda prie ilgalaikės BŽŪP vizijos ir ilgalaikių tikslų įgyvendinimo?

Ar šiame kontekste Komisija pripažįsta, kad Lietuvos pateikta papildoma informacija buvo ir išlieka nepatenkinama, o ją priėmusiems ir SP patvirtinusiems AGRI DG pareigūnams taip pat tenka atsakomybė už skandalingus rezultatus?
at: (English version) to the Commission Bronis Ropė (Verts/ALE) (10 April 2024) Subject: Farmers’ participation in eco-schemes According to the Commission, the greening requirements developed by the Commission have been implemented by around 96% of Lithuanian farmers. According to data from the eco-schemes developed by the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Lithuania, only 26 000 out of 114 000 applicants participated in the area eco-schemes (23%). In its observation No 65 on the Lithuanian strategic plan, the Commission stated: ‘Lithuania should review and, where relevant, redesign its proposed eco-schemes to improve the practices included and focus on those interventions that have a higher environmental value. This would reduce the potential risk that the funds allocated are scattered among many interventions and thus lose their effectiveness and that farmers mostly subscribe to the least ambitious ones.’ (1) Pursuant to Article 118(3) of Regulation 2021/2115, ‘(t)he Member State shall provide to the Commission all necessary additional information and, where appropriate, revise the proposed plan.’ Could the Commission please answer the following questions: 1.
Did the Commission envisage that three out of four Lithuanian farmers would not participate in the eco-schemes?
Do they contribute to the long-term vision and objectives of the CAP?

In this context, does the Commission acknowledge that the additional information provided by Lithuania was and remains unsatisfactory, and that the officials of DG AGRI who received it and approved the strategic plan also bear responsibility for the scandalous results?

(29 May 2024) The Commission is not familiar with the figure cited by the Honourable Member on the number of applicants for support for eco-schemes in Lithuania. According to the information provided by the Lithuanian authorities in the 2023 Annual Performance Report on the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plan, the number of applications under the eco-schemes was almost 62 000, covering 82% of the total area declared for the Basic Income Support Scheme (BISS). The Commission considers that, overall, this is a reasonable outcome, given that 2023 was the first year of the implementation of the new CAP and of eco-schemes as a new voluntary instrument. Certain challenges were however observed with variable uptake between individual eco-schemes. The lower overall number of applications for the eco-schemes as compared to BISS may reflect differences in farm structure within the country. The Commission considers the eco-schemes as a key tool for delivering the CAP’s contribution to EU environmental and climate goals. In this context, the Commission has carefully examined the additional information provided by the Lithuanian authorities during the approval of its CAP Strategic Plan and concluded that it was sufficient, as the number and design of eco-schemes was in the first instance a policy choice of the Member State based on the needs’ analysis. Under shared management, the Commission will continue to follow-up with the Lithuanian authorities the implementation of the Plan, the progress towards its objectives and targets, including the performance of eco-schemes. Certain related changes have already been proposed by the Lithuanian authorities and were approved by the Commission in the second amendment of the Plan in April 2024.
